title: Spawn 10,000 tasks that yield once and join them
summary: Spawn 10,000 tasks on one thread, each of which yields once and then works out a value from its index, wait for every one of them through its handle, and return the sum of their values.
notes: An asynchronous task on one thread: each operation is one awaited call that spawns 10,000 tasks on the executor that runs it and ends when every task has been joined. A task only yields once and computes one small integer, so the figures are the cost of spawning a task, scheduling it twice and joining it: the executor's own machinery, not any work in the tasks. No timer or sleep with a real delay is involved. Rust runs on each crate's own single-thread executor, Go with GOMAXPROCS=1, Python on one asyncio loop, JavaScript on its event loop.
